reason: All reachable startup candidates are implemented, source/fresh validated, and mutation checked at the implementation commit; only the explicitly excluded runtime and impossible-build arms remain bounded.

boundary.startingEvent: Startup parses an OPTIONS=boulder statement, optionally alongside primary/Rogue symbol-set selections and S_boulder overrides.
boundary.endingEvent: Configuration errors are dismissed and startup continues through the first tutorial map, or the accepted boulder value is shown in #optionsfull and on that map.
boundary.validInputs: Missing and empty values; literal, control, decimal, octal, hexadecimal, C-style, caret, meta, and multi-byte spellings; printable nonclashing bytes; default monster-class and warning-symbol clashes; repetitions and source-permitted orderings with symset, roguesymset, SYMBOLS, and ROGUESYMBOLS.
boundary.observables: Exact configuration-error text and raw wait, primary and Rogue override bytes, active showsyms and menu value, first tutorial-map glyph, complete screens and attributes, cursors, persisted startup state, and unchanged PRNG order.
boundary.exclusions: Runtime optfn_boulder(do_set) redraw on an already-created level, interactive symbol-set handlers, Rogue-level entry after startup, non-BACKWARD_COMPAT builds, and map behavior after the first tutorial rendering/#optionsfull boundary.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: cfgfiles.c cnf_line_OPTIONS(), options.c parseoptions()/optfn_boulder()/string_for_opt()/escapes()/initoptions_finish(), drawing.c def_char_to_monclass(), and symbols.c get_othersym()/switch_symbols().
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: The generated optlist.h boulder row fixes parser eligibility; defsym.h/drawing.c define the exhaustive default monster, warning, object, and S_boulder symbols; the generated symbol-set catalog fixes selectable primary/Rogue sets.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Traced every optfn_boulder request arm and do_set branch, first-byte escape families, first-match monster lookup, warning range, override writes, initial-vs-runtime split, end-of-configuration get_othersym application, menu serialization, and boulder display consumption.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: Searched js/options.js generic compound fallback and menu guard, js/symbols.js escape/operation/override tables, js/jsmain.js startup ordering, js/fruit.js partial initoptions_finish(), js/display.js boulder redirect, generated symbol data, focused parser/menu/display tests, and the compound diagnostic census.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The pinned BACKWARD_COMPAT TTY build rejects decoded NUL and high-bit 0xB0 through the signed-char control branch. Runtime redraw and later Rogue-level consumption remain excluded.

entries.candidate: boulder parser dispatch, negation, duplicate, and mandatory-value handling
entries.reachability: The generated CompOpt row accepts boulder during startup; missing/empty values and negated spellings reach parseoptions()/string_for_opt() before any symbol write.
entries.effects: Reports source parser errors, preserves duplicate bookkeeping, and avoids writes for rejected statements.
entries.evidence: include/optlist.h boulder row; options.c parseoptions() and optfn_boulder(do_set); scripts/config-error.test.mjs currently records three owed diagnostics.

entries.reachability: Every nonempty boulder value is expanded in place before validation; only the first decoded byte is subsequently read.
entries.owner: js/options_escapes.js options.c:escapes() port consumed by js/options.js and js/symbols.js
entries.effects: Selects the byte that validation and both override writes observe, without randomness or output by itself.
entries.evidence: options.c escapes() and optfn_boulder(); js/options_escapes.js ports the full expansion and scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs pins literal, caret, decimal, octal, hex, C-style, meta, trailing-prefix, NUL, and multi-byte families.

entries.reachability: Caret or numeric escape syntax can make the first decoded byte lower than space, including NUL.
entries.effects: Reports the control-character diagnostic without changing either override table; an earlier accepted boulder byte remains intact.
entries.evidence: Fresh patched-C OPTIONS=boulder:^@ and literal OPTIONS=boulder:\0 both report exactly 'boulder symbol cannot be a control character.' with zero RNG. An earlier accepted boulder:0 remains visible as [0], proving the source reset comment stale and the executable < ' ' branch authoritative.

entries.reachability: A decoded byte matching any def_monsyms entry from index 1 through MAXMCLASSES-1 reaches the first-match clash arm.
entries.owner: js/options.js optfn_boulder startup arm with a generated/default symbol lookup
entries.effects: Adds Badoption with visctrl(byte) and the monster label, leaving both override tables unchanged.
entries.evidence: drawing.c def_monsyms[]/def_char_to_monclass(); options.c optfn_boulder(); defsym.h generated monster-symbol universe.

entries.reachability: A decoded byte from '1' through WARNCOUNT-1+'0' that did not match a monster class reaches the warning arm; warning level zero is intentionally outside the range.
entries.effects: Adds Badoption with visctrl(byte) and the warning label, leaving both override tables unchanged.
entries.evidence: options.c optfn_boulder(); drawing.c def_warnsyms[]; include/sym.h WARNCOUNT 6.

entries.reachability: A decoded byte at least space which matches neither a default monster symbol nor warning levels 1 through 5 reaches the success arm.
entries.owner: js/options.js parse result plus js/symbols.js ordered startup operations
entries.effects: Writes the same byte to go.ov_primary_syms and go.ov_rogue_syms at S_boulder and emits no diagnostic.
entries.evidence: options.c optfn_boulder success arm; js/options.js emits an ordered boulder operation and the focused symbol test proves it writes the same byte to both C-owned override tables.

entries.candidate: high-bit decoded byte under the pinned C build
entries.reachability: Meta syntax or a UTF-8/config byte can produce a first byte at least 0x80 before opts[0] comparisons.
entries.effects: The pinned signed-char build promotes the decoded byte as negative and reports the control-character diagnostic without a write.
entries.evidence: Fresh patched-C OPTIONS=boulder:\M0 decodes 0xB0, reports exactly 'boulder symbol cannot be a control character.', and consumes zero RNG before dismissal; focused tests also pin the 0x80 boundary.

entries.candidate: right-to-left OPTIONS ordering and repeated boulder values
entries.reachability: Multiple comma-separated options and repeated configuration statements can select boulder alongside symset and S_boulder assignments.
entries.effects: Replays accepted override writes in source parse order; rejected values leave the prior accepted byte intact.
entries.evidence: options.c parseoptions() recursion/order, optfn_boulder writes, and the existing ordered symbolOperations seam.

entries.candidate: primary/Rogue symset selection around the dual boulder override
entries.reachability: Valid symset/roguesymset selection can precede or follow boulder configuration during initial option processing.
entries.effects: Set selection changes base tables and metadata without erasing explicit boulder overrides; the primary and Rogue slots retain the same configured byte.
entries.evidence: options.c optfn_boulder; symbols.c init/select/switch behavior; completed ordered symbolOperations implementation.

entries.reachability: Every normal startup calls initoptions_finish() after all configuration and symbol-set processing while go.opt_initial is true.
entries.effects: Copies the final nonzero primary boulder override into gs.showsyms after all ordered symbol operations and before map rendering.
entries.evidence: options.c initoptions_finish(); symbols.c get_othersym(); js/jsmain.js startup order; js/fruit.js currently ports only the fruit-owned part.

entries.reachability: The O/m options menu calls optfn_boulder(get_val) after startup configuration.
entries.effects: Shows the explicit primary override, or the active rock-class fallback when none exists, without refusing the menu.
entries.evidence: options.c optfn_boulder(get_val); boulder is removed from UNPARSED_COMPOUND_OPTIONS and scripts/options-menu.test.mjs pins the configured live value.

entries.reachability: OPTIONS=tutorial loads dat/tut-1.lua, whose fixed boulder at (25,12) is visible near the starting hero before any gameplay command.
entries.owner: js/display.js object glyph redirect consuming gs.showsyms[S_boulder]
entries.effects: Renders the configured accepted byte in the first complete map with unchanged screens, cursors, and PRNG sequence otherwise.
entries.evidence: dat/tut-1.lua fixed boulder; display.c/object glyph path; js/display.js already redirects BOULDER to misc_symbol(SYM_BOULDER).

entries.reachability: Requires do_set after go.opt_initial has cleared, through an interactive in-game option change.
entries.effects: First effect is an immediate active-set get_othersym write and go.opt_need_redraw after this startup boundary.
entries.evidence: options.c optfn_boulder !go.opt_initial branch; selected boundary starts only from configuration parsing.

entries.reachability: Requires compiling without BACKWARD_COMPAT, but the patched reference and supported port build define it.
entries.effects: No reachable effect in the pinned build.
entries.evidence: options.c defines BACKWARD_COMPAT locally before the optfn_boulder preprocessor split; optlist.h does the same for the generated row.

sourceReview: Source-derived implementation now covers all twelve reachable startup families from parseoptions()/optfn_boulder()/escapes() through drawing.c def_char_to_monclass(), dual primary/Rogue overrides, source-order symbol operations, symbols.c get_othersym(), initoptions_finish(), #optionsfull, and the fixed first tutorial-map boulder. Fresh patched C settled the stale NUL-reset comment in favor of the executable control rejection and pinned signed high-bit 0xB0 rejection. The final eight-segment comparison matched 21,168 PRNG calls and 125 screens/cursors with zero animation frames. The runtime redraw arm remains later and the non-BACKWARD_COMPAT arm cannot occur in the pinned build.
